public_rationale: Marcus said GPT-5 still had his long-cited problems, and he named chess rule-following as the example. On August 7, 2025, Mathieu Acher showed that GPT-5 and GPT-5 Thinking both played an illegal move after a short four-move opening, as earlier GPT models had done. GPT-5 Thinking kept the illegal move even after being told it was illegal. That fits the claim that these failures lingered. OpenAI did report fewer hallucinations, so some problems shrank. But the claim says the problems were still there, not that nothing improved.
limitations: The main evidence is a single demonstration, not a benchmark.
Acher himself warns against over-interpreting one chess example.
The broader 'quarter century' list of problems is not tested here item by item.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-5 still has the longstanding problems Marcus has identified, such as chess rule-following and world models.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Systematic tests of launch-era GPT-5 show it reliably follows chess rules and keeps a consistent board state, with no such failures.
